title: Mexican Chicken & Grain Bowls
description: Spiced chicken strips over warm grain salad with fresh tomato and crisp lettuce.

steps.text: Dice the tomatoes and tear the lettuce into bite-size pieces. Set aside.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken strips for 6–8 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through.
Warm the grain salad in a small pan or the microwave for 1–2 minutes and fluff it with a fork.
Build the bowls: grain base, chicken, tomato, lettuce. Finish with a squeeze of lime and a pinch of cumin or paprika.

notes: Eat within a day: the chicken and lettuce are on a short date.

title: Pan-Seared Salmon & Cod with Tomato Salad
description: Two fish, one pan, ten minutes. Butter-basted and served on a lemony salad.

steps.text: Pat the fish dry with paper towel and season both sides with salt and pepper.
Melt the butter in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Cook the salmon skin-side down 4 minutes, flip and cook 2–3 more. Cook the cod 3 minutes per side.
While the fish cooks, slice the tomatoes and toss with the lettuce, olive oil, lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Plate the fish over the salad and spoon the pan butter over the top.

notes: Cod is more delicate than salmon: flip it once, gently.

title: Butter-Basted Steak with Tomato & Lettuce
description: A fast pan-seared steak with a simple salad. Cook it tomorrow or freeze it tonight.

steps.text: Take the steak out of the fridge 20 minutes ahead. Pat dry and season generously with salt and pepper.
Sear in a very hot pan with the oil for 2–3 minutes per side for medium-rare. Add the butter in the last minute and baste.
Rest the steak 5 minutes under foil, then slice against the grain.
Slice the tomatoes, toss with the lettuce, a little olive oil and salt, and serve with the steak.

notes: Thin cuts cook fast; use the 2–3 minute guide and check by touch.

title: Banana Croissant Bread Pudding
description: Uses up the extra croissants and the very ripe bananas in one warm dessert.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and butter a baking dish.
Tear the croissants into chunks and spread them in the dish.
Slice the ripe bananas and tuck the slices between the croissant pieces.
Whisk the eggs, milk, sugar and vanilla (add a little grated ginger if you like). Pour over, press down gently and let it soak 10 minutes.
Bake for about 30 minutes, until golden on top and just set in the middle. Serve warm.

notes: Croissants freeze well: freeze the rest of the bag tonight.
